title: Trunk EMG in static load holding
summary: Simulate each static holding task and report trunk muscle activation (%MVC) under each electrode site.
simulate: Scale the model to the study subject (table below).
Set the static posture and hand-load position (height, distance, asymmetry) of the task.
Apply the load: hand mass, or an external pull at the chest (pull direction, moment).
Solve muscle forces; report activation under each electrode, normalised as the study did.
Keep sides apart where given (left/right); else average both sides.

outputs.label: EMG
outputs.definition: EMG = surface EMG amplitude under the electrode, % of the study's maximal-exertion reference (MVC)

notes: EMG references differ: max over 6 maximal exertions (Ghezelbash, Larivière), baseline-subtracted max of 4 MVCs (Lavender), McGill MVCs (Granata).
Ghezelbash 2020 loads were turned to the subject's left (left = same side). Chest pulls: 0° = forward pull (extensor demand), 90° = to the right.
Dynamic lifts and unloaded bending are not here (see flexion_relaxation).
agent_prompt: You are validating a trunk musculoskeletal model against surface EMG in static load holding. For each task scale the model to the subject of the study in its `studies` (see `subjects`), set the posture and load, solve for muscle forces and report the activation (%) of the fascicles under the named electrode and side. Electrodes: LG longissimus, IC iliocostalis, MF multifidus, ES erector spinae, RA rectus abdominis, EO / IO external / internal oblique; the vertebra in brackets is the electrode level. Ghezelbash 2020 (g20_*): 14 kg in both hands, held 0.2 x body height in front of the feet at the stated height, knees straight; trunk flexion 18.3° (umbilicus), 50.5° (mid-femur), 68.1° (knee), 92.1° (mid-tibia) (Ghezelbash 2024 Fig 3c); asymmetric tasks: the load is turned asymmetry_deg to the subject's left at mid-femur height (left = ipsilateral). Larivière 2019 (lar19_*): trunk vertical, bar in both hands at L5/S1 height ~20-23 cm in front of L5/S1 (P1), at shoulder height close to the chest (P2), or at shoulder height with arms extended (P3); left and right averaged. Lavender 1992 (lav_*): upright, pelvis fixed; a horizontal force at the chest harness (scapula-tip height) giving 50 Nm about L3-L4; pull_dir_deg 0 = pulling the trunk forward (extensors work), 90 = pulling to the subject's right, 180 = pulling backward. Granata 2005 (gra_*): upright, pelvis fixed; horizontal force at T10 of 100, 135 and 170 N, pull 0 = forward (extension effort), 180 = backward (flexion effort); report the mean activation over the three forces, left and right averaged. Normalise each muscle as its study did: Ghezelbash and Larivière = its maximum over six maximal exertions (flexion, extension, left/right lateral bending, left/right axial rotation); Lavender = (task - relaxed upright) / (maximum of four MVCs: flexion, extension, left and right twist - relaxed upright) x 100; Granata = maximum over MVCs in flexion, extension, left/right lateral bending and twist. Do not tune the model to these data. Return one JSON object following answer_format: {task id: {output key: value}} in the units given there; use null for tasks you cannot simulate.
